newsitem.title: UK: Tobacco companies hide low-tar vents, expert says.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco companies hide low-tar vents, expert says.

text.p: Many smokers who buy low-tar and low-nicotine cigarettes are unwittingly ruining the effect by blocking tiny holes in the filter with their fingers, U.S. researchers said on Wednesday. Behaviour expert Dr Lynn Kozlowski and colleagues at Penn State University found up to 40 percent of smokers surveyed did not know the holes, called filter vents, were what made the cigarettes "light".
Blocking the vents with the fingers could double the amount of tar and nicotine inhaled, Kozlowski wrote in the British Medical Association journal Tobacco Control.

She accused the cigarette industry of deliberately keeping the design a secret so that smokers would stay hooked. "The cigarette industry has acknowledged that vent-blocking can happen, but disputes the prevalence of the problem," she wrote.
At the very least, the vents could be made more visible, she said. Last year, nearly 60 percent of cigarettes sold in the United States were low-tar, Kozlowski said.
